newsitem.title: Belgium: Belgian police discount lead in serial killer case.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police discount lead in serial killer case.

text.p: The man leading a police search for a serial killer in Belgium denied on Tuesday that a suspect had been identified.
The police hunt began after the discovery in Mons, Belgium, of bin bags containing the surgically severed body parts of four women.
"At the moment we have no objective evidence that allows us to follow up this lead," Mons Public Prosecutor Pierre Honore told RTBF television.
Belgian media reported earlier that police inquiries were focused on a man who had contacted them in a different part of the country before attempting to kill himself.

Belgian police have so far found 11 plastic rubbish sacks containing severed body parts since the chance discovery in a ditch next to the Brussels-Paris railway line on Saturday of bags containing arms and legs.
So far no heads and only one torso have been found.
Honore told RTBF the search of the area had now been widened, with more officers and a police helicopter scouring the area for further clues.
"We can say almost certainly it was the work of one person," Honore said, noting the precise and identical way in which the bodies had been cut up.
All the remains have been transferred to Liege University hospital where forensic pathologists have the task of piecing together the anatomical jigsaw.
Belgian newspapers on Tuesday named several women who have gone missing in the area as possible victims, but Honore said identification of the victims would take some time.
Belgian Police have said there was no immediate reason to suspect a link with gruesome discoveries made in a paedophile scandal which has rocked the country in the past nine months.
